convoLines.text: "What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed? Happy?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"I don't answer that one myself. Not yet. Maybe when I've decided whether surviving counts as an excuse or just a reason."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want the truth? I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. I was ashamed of the truth. Out here nobody asks, so I stopped telling. Happy now?"
"That again?" Zuri sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want the truth? I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be in charge. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around. Happy now?"
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Zuri rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Zuri says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I asked Fernando about what scares you most — Fernando's gone. What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on what scares you most."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Fernando always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I sleep in short shifts. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About that question — What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing. Don't make me repeat it."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on what you're hoping for."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Since Fernando died... I keep expecting to see Fernando at the fire. Stupid."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I keep turning over the last thing Fernando said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Fernando. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Actually, forget it."
"...Where was I? Gone. Ask me something else."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 3 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.' Give it time."
They light up a little when they see you.
"Nobody says Fernando's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I'm picking up Fernando's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Oh! Oh — Still on what's been happening."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
You show them Jewelweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What? We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
Zuri has an edge today — something curdled.
"This one — Chinese Chestnut. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Good question." "Rahul? I'd trust Rahul with my pack. That's the highest compliment I have."
"Rahul was a dockworker, before. You can still see it — the way they handle things."
"Has it changed? Everything changes. Ask me again after the next hard week."
"Still on the others."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Gertrudis — The Pit, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Hey — I found some Jewelweed today. You were right, it was right where you said."
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
You show them Chinese Chestnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Pit. They just... took Gertrudis. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can I tell you something? I've been writing letters I'll never send. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. James doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Burdock today. You were right, it was right where you said."
You can feel the history in how they greet you.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "I dreamed Diego was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to trading knowledge."
"...Where was I? Gone. Ask me something else."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching? Simple as that."
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving. That's the whole of it."
"Watch the quiet ones. Not the loud — the loud tell you everything. The quiet are either thinking or planning, and you can't tell which until it matters."
"Still on your read on people here."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Let's move."
"Good question." "Gauntlet. They just... took Giulia. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie. How are you holding up, though?"
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Right. Still on needing to be alone."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"Okay." Giulia looks down. "Okay, you got me. I wasn't a comic shop owner. I was a crossing guard. If the wrong people know, it doesn't fall on me. It falls on them." Their voice is small.
Giulia looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"We went over this," Giulia says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

d41: 🕯️ The treeline is still torn up from the raid when the System's light comes for them. Nobody is ready. The light doesn't wait.

recoverHome: d41: That night, they bring Fernando home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d40: At the grave, Zuri, Rahul, Gertrudis and 7 more speak for Diego — "Fernando trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d41: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.

d42: ◈ SYSTEM: "GRANARY: SEALED. Cool, dark, and full of waiting food. Twenty-four mouths. You are not a camp anymore. You are a going concern. The audience has already commissioned the famine episode. We told them there would not be one."
d42: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.

d44: You bury Fernando. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+6 trauma)
